$$s^3 = (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3})(5+2\sqrt{6}) = 5\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{12} + 5\sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{18}.$$

Since $2\sqrt{12} = 4\sqrt{3}$ and $2\sqrt{18} = 6\sqrt{2}$, this gives

$$s^3 = 11\sqrt{2} + 9\sqrt{3}.$$

So $a = 11$, $b = 9$, $c = 0$. The representation is unique because $\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{3}$, and $\sqrt{6}$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. A numerical check agrees: $(3.14626)^3 \approx 31.14$, and $11\sqrt{2} + 9\sqrt{3} \approx 31.14$.
